q1.answer: The left side (split in the lip and gum on the left).

q2.answer: In the bone under the pink gum, in the bone that holds the teeth; the gap runs from the floor of the nose down to the gum.

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the left front tooth. About half of children with a cleft do not have it.

q4.answer: The eye tooth waits high in the bone and needs bone to grow into, so the graft gives it bone to come down through.

q7.answer: New bone now fills the gap from the floor of the nose to the gum, joining the two parts of the upper jaw, and the gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is still in the bone and starts moving down toward the new bone.

q8.answer: With an X-ray at about 3 to 6 months, which shows how well the new bone has taken.

q9.answer: The hip can be sore for a while after surgery.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone into the row of teeth. Some get stuck and need a small operation.

q12.answer: Braces move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it; or keep the gap with a false tooth on a removable plate; or, once growth has stopped, an implant or a bridge. The cleft team helps choose.
